gist: England beat New Zealand 37-12 in a repeat of last year.
England played with a more fluid and less predictable style.
New Zealand struggled after a long and tiring schedule.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: England secured a 37-12 victory over New Zealand in front of 81,953 fans. Unlike last year when they relied heavily on kicking, England played a more fluid passing game and scored tries through clever movement. Ben Earl made 33 carries, while the forward pack and defence dominated the match against a depleted visiting side.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Steve Borthwick's team has experienced many false dawns and fluctuating form over four years. This win suggests England may have developed a more sustainable tactical approach and deeper squad balance to challenge rugby superpowers ahead of next year's World Cup.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: New Zealand will face England again next Saturday at Allianz Stadium in the Nations Championship third-place play-off. Meanwhile, England's next major challenge will be an away match against Ireland in the Six Nations tournament next February.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Australia edged past Wales in a tight contest at the Principality Stadium. Tries from Taniela Tupou, Brandon Paenga-Amosa, Max Jorgensen and Len Ikitau helped the visitors build a lead. Wales responded through captain Dewi Lake who scored twice, alongside a try from Blair Murray, but Australia ultimately held on for the win.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The victory ended a four-match losing run for Australia and secured the Nations Championship spoils. For Wales, the defeat highlighted missed attacking opportunities after they failed to capitalise on their chances following their previous notable win against New Zealand.

gist: James Harden scored 51 points in a victory against the Indiana Pacers.
Harden surpassed Kobe Bryant for third place in all-time 50-point NBA games.
The 37-year-old recorded his 26th career 50-point performance during the NBA Cup.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: James Harden scored 51 points for the Cleveland Cavaliers in a 128-119 win against the Indiana Pacers. This performance marked his 26th career 50-point game, moving him past Kobe Bryant into third place on the all-time list. Harden, aged 37, also contributed six rebounds and six assists at Rocket Arena.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The achievement places Harden behind only Wilt Chamberlain and Michael Jordan in NBA history for 50-point games. Harden described the milestone as humbling and special, noting the difficulty of maintaining such impact in his 18th season.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: The Cleveland Cavaliers are scheduled to play the Chicago Bulls on Tuesday.

gist: Andriy Shevchenko accused Mykhailo Mudryk's camp of seeking a false scapegoat for a doping test.
Mudryk blamed the Ukrainian Association of Football for his failed test and subsequent 20-month ban.
Shevchenko denied the allegations, defending the association and asking Mudryk to retract his comments.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Andriy Shevchenko stated that Mykhailo Mudryk's representatives repeatedly asked for a football federation employee to falsely take the blame for Mudryk's positive test for meldonium. Mudryk, suspended from November 2024 to July 2026, blamed the Ukrainian Association of Football for the failed test, claiming it happened on international duty and criticizing a lack of support.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Shevchenko called the claims baseless slander and defended the professionalism of association staff, while Mudryk argued the handling of the matter delayed his return to football.
